notes:
Summary: Sailfish Codecraft builds an IDE-centric copilot for enterprise dev teams (plugins for VS Code and JetBrains). Primary ask: repo-aware context retrieval with strict residency and low streaming latency. They want embeddings-per-repo, incremental chunking (overlap control), and an affordable persistent vector DB that can be private/VPC or on-prem. Quote/paraphrase: 'We need under 50ms per streaming token for interactive completions at peak, and model versions pinned per workspace so customers can opt for high-accuracy or low-cost quantized variants.'

Key technical points captured during calls:
- Workload: interactive completion + multi-file search + explain/code-review; many short-turn chats (avg 3-5 msgs) from IDE plugin.
- Throughput targets: 80-120 concurrent active editors per cluster initially; burst to 300. Target 20k tokens/min sustained across fleet.
- Latency SLOs: 30-100ms per token for streaming path; 200ms for non-streaming multi-chunk rerank.
- Embeddings strategy: per-repo dense vectors, incremental indexing when commits land; prefer 512-d or 1536-d depending on model. Careful about chunk size (200-800 tokens) and overlap 10-15% to preserve context.
- Vector DB: evaluation will compare managed RedisVector (hosted/dedicated) vs self-hosted Milvus on-prem. Requirement: encryption at rest + backup snapshot retention policy.
- Model preferences: open models first (Llama2-70B quantized for copilot latency; Falcon for summarization), with option to bring custom fine-tunes. Must support model pinning per workspace and automatic fallback to smaller variants when capacity constrained.
- Security/compliance: EU-only data residency for EU customers, SSO/SAML, audit logs per token/route, HSM-backed KMS for keys. Retention controls per customer and ability to purge vectors on request.

POC ask: 2-week dedicated POC — ingest 5 large repos (private), run retrieval/embedding pipeline, measure end-to-end latency for IDE streaming + cold-hit vector recall. Redwood to provide an SOW and dedicated infra sizing.

Notes shorthand/CRM style: 'SE to deliver POC runbook by 2024-11-07; legal needs KMS appendix; Alex to confirm GPU type (A10G vs A100) and estimate monthly committed spend; customer leaning Private (on-prem) for EU accounts.'
